## 3. The evidence that moved it



**The month's strongest result is a claim of harm, not a null.**
*JCO* published TrilynX, the placebo-controlled phase 3 of the IAP antagonist
xevinapant ([40902136](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40902136/)), alongside a
commentary whose title is the finding:
[SMAC mimetics accelerate progression of locally advanced head and neck cancer](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40902135/).
A decade of preclinical apoptosis-sensitisation enthusiasm produced a randomized
trial in which the intervention arm did worse. Failed is common; worse is rare,
and worse is what makes a class dead rather than mis-targeted.

**Cancer Discovery published a coordinated argument against the cell type it was
simultaneously publishing engineering papers about.** Three titles in one issue —
[The Dark Side of NK Cells](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40904100/),
[cytotoxic NK cells impede checkpoint response](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40530504/),
and [tumour-associated NK cells contribute to ICB resistance](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40530506/) —
against a rewiring review, a multiplex-edited CAR-NK and a loop-CAR iNK in the
same month. The engineering is preclinical and phase 1; the negative biology is
from human checkpoint cohorts. This is the month that made
`suppressive-population-inversion` a thread rather than a recurring oddity.

**Tertiary lymphoid structures contradicted themselves inside one journal.**
[40992783](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40992783/) links TLS to immunotherapy
response in Merkel cell carcinoma; [40998518](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40998518/)
finds high Treg and PMN-MDSC density in TLS to be a hallmark of *fatal* cervical
cancer. Same month, same journal. TLS presence alone cannot be a predictive
biomarker if both hold, and the composition — not the structure — is what carries
the signal.

**Checkpoints: the field ran out of nouns.** Zero of May's five nominated targets
and zero of June's five appear. September nominates no replacement roster at all.
The only checkpoint content with momentum is LAG-3, and it is follow-up analysis
of an agent that already cleared phase 3
([40638872](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40638872/)). No newly nominated
checkpoint entered a phase 1 anywhere.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

The NK block above, plus
[40954074](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40954074/): MAIT cells, generally
proposed as innate-like antitumour effectors, promote progression and Treg
accumulation in bladder tumours. And
[40929245](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40929245/): an interferon-induced
senescent CD8 state reduces anti-PD-1 efficacy, which removes both CD8
infiltration and the interferon signature as benefit predictors in the same
sentence.

[40983343](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40983343/) (*JITC*) attacks ctDNA as a
surrogate directly: the association between early ctDNA change and overall
survival depends on which molecular-response cutoff and which collection
timepoints are chosen. Every ctDNA-surrogate paper in this corpus now has to
answer it.

[40828134](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40828134/) (*JEM*) — antibiotics
unleash neuroinflammation — is filed as a refutation on the neuro-immune thread
rather than a support, because it removes the assumption that microbiome
depletion is an inert experimental manipulation. A large fraction of this
thread's mouse work uses antibiotic depletion as its control arm.

### (b) Method credibility

Eight cards, the largest single-month block in the corpus. Three concern
reagents rather than analyses, which is the more damaging kind:
[stable Cas9 expression alters cell growth independently of editing](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41020501/),
[AsCas12a tolerates insertions in target DNA](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40966510/),
and [accurate tandem-repeat detection exposes ubiquitous sequence reuse](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40923760/).

[40963104](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40963104/) states that scATAC-seq
analysis discards finer-resolution information — in a modality most downstream
methods treat as solved.

[40715786](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40715786/) names over-reliance on AI
code assistants as a threat to scientific software. It is the loudest agentic-AI
paper of the month, and it is a warning.

Two further retractions of record: the
[CB1 agonist-bound crystal structures](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40866714/)
and [live-imaging claims about kinetic genome organization](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40966347/).
